This is the rider's own best point and it is partly right: under RD-5 a specified-road authorisation reaches only that road and no fact ties any driven segment to Upper Paya Lebar Road, so that limb fails - but the same evidence leaves the scope to be read as a general route choice, and RD-5/G13 at most make it undetermined rather than an automatic full-refund finding.

F15 (no incidents) is conceded as far as RD-4(a) goes, but C4 ignores F13 and F14: while Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway sat at band 2, 10-19 km/h, from 22:40 (F12), the alternative corridors ran at band 5, 40-49 km/h (F13, F14), which is exactly the "reasonable cause" RD-4(b) preserves as corroboration and is the basis on which F8's request was made.

C5 proves my sizing point rather than the rider's: F4 bills $7.50 for 5.32 km at $1.4102/km while F3's segment adds only 5.04 km, so the recoverable mileage cannot exceed 5.04 x $1.4102 = $7.11, and F7's base, time and platform lines are not routing items at all.

I do not resist the $7.11 figure - it is the same cap my brief requests - but the rider is wrong that "anything wrongly added" falls: under RD-3(c) the $0.11 meter waiting unit (F5) is chargeable and non-refundable on RydeTAXI, and F6 (surge 1.0x) simply confirms no surge line exists to remove.

RD-6 requires an already-upheld route dispute in the 90-day window and F18 itself records route: 0 with the 1 upheld dispute not being a route case, so this case cannot make the history "repeated"; F17 and F18 are profile facts and may support a flag_account request only, never the main finding.
